title: observability-weekly-2026-06-15
content:
Observability Team - Weekly Notes (2026-06-15)
Owner: Priya Nair
Attendees: Priya, Liam, Gabriela, Marcus, Erin (SRE sync), Ben (Serving-runtime)

TL;DR
- Tracing: finalized sampling proposal for low-volume customers; started rollout to staging for SDK v1.4.
- Dashboards: new cost-per-route dashboard prototype is live in staging; still tuning aggregation windows.
- Cost telemetry: initial TPU/GPU token-cost attribution spike analysis points to a misconfigured batching policy on dedicated clusters (OBS-214).
- Action items: instrumentation rollout checklist, alert tuning, and a small migration script for backend tag normalization.

This week (high level)
- Tracing
  - Completed RFC review for adaptive sampling (@Gabriela). Decided to use a hybrid approach: per-customer sampling config with global fallback at 0.1% for free tier and 1% for paid tiers.
  - SDK v1.4 (tracing + auto-instrumentation) deployed to staging. Smoke tests show spans for generation-start/generation-end and function/tool-call boundaries. Need to add explicit trace attributes for model_variant and quantization_profile.
  - Work items: OBS-198 Add model_variant tag to span (in progress, PR linked).
  - Blockers: one flaky test around context propagation on async workers (Marcus investigating).

- Dashboards
  - Cost-per-route prototype: Liam built a dashboard aggregating GPU hours, token counts, and per-route unit cost. Early findings show ~18% higher cost on certain reranking routes due to long context windows.
  - Metrics/visuals: added p50/p95 latency and error-rate overlays to the same dashboard to correlate cost vs latency. Need to add cost anomaly banding (monthly baseline +/- stdev).
  - Ask from platform: export dashboard CSV for finance extraction (~weekly export) — Liam to add a scheduled export job.

- Cost telemetry
  - Investigation (OBS-214): a sudden token-cost spike on 6/12 traced to a dedicate cluster autoscaling policy that provisioned larger GPU instances without appropriate batching config. Temporary mitigation: scale-down policy applied and manual reconfiguration of batching window.
  - Next steps: automated alert for unexpected cost-by-cluster deviation (>20% day-over-day) and a postmortem doc.

Standups / daily notes
- Mon 6/15: Quick sync. Priya: finalize rollout checklist. Gabriela: tests for adaptive sampler. Liam: dashboard joins with Finance. Marcus: async propagation fix.
- Tue 6/16: Cross-team with Serving-runtime to standardize model_variant attribute names. Agreement to use "model_variant" and "quant_profile" as canonical tags.
- Wed 6/17: SRE sync re: alert noise. Decided to raise thresholds for non-prod clusters and add suppression window for deploys.

Action items (owners & rough ETA)
- Priya: Finalize instrumentation rollout checklist + risk matrix (ETA 6/18).
- Gabriela: Complete unit/integration tests for adaptive sampling and fix flaky async test (OBS-198) (ETA 6/19).
- Liam: Add CSV export job and cost anomaly band to dashboard (ETA 6/22).
- Marcus: Patch for context propagation; open PR and run extended integration tests (ETA 6/17).
- Erin (SRE): Create alert for cost-by-cluster deviation and link to runbook (ETA 6/18).

Risks / blockers
- Flaky context-propagation test delaying tracing rollout to staging -> production. If not resolved by 6/19, we will proceed with a partial rollout that excludes async-heavy services.
- Cost spikes from Dedicated clusters remain a medium risk until automated guardrails are in place. Finance flagged this as priority.

Notes from cross-team discussions
- Serving-runtime: will add the model_variant/quant_profile metadata to the inference response headers for easier downstream correlation. Expected code change in their next sprint.
- Console/Product: requested a per-customer cost breakdown panel for the console (product ticket created). We scoped an MVP that uses nightly batch exports.

Open questions
- Sampling: do we allow customers to override sampling rate via API keys? (Privacy and compliance check required)
- Cost attribution: should we attribute shared caching savings proportionally by route usage or by request count? Proposed to start with proportional-by-tokens and re-evaluate after 2 weeks.

Meetings planned next week
- Wed 6/17 9:30am: Tracing rollout sync w/ Serving-runtime (invite sent).
- Thu 6/18 11:00am: Cost telemetry postmortem planning with Finance & Platform.
- Fri 6/19 4:00pm: Retrospective on dashboard prototype and next steps.

Appendix (quick links)
- Tracing roadmap (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Tracing+Roadmap
- OBS-214 (cost spike): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-214
- OBS-198 (model_variant tagging): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-198
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/87

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Explore using short-lived sampling overrides when debug flag is set (avoid persistent high-volume tracing in prod).
- Consider a daily reduced-resolution sample (1% of spans) for long-term storage to support trend analysis without retaining full fidelity.
- Follow up with Platform infra on enabling per-cluster cost export to BigQuery for richer analysis.

End of notes.
